title: [TTK-01] CRUD on a real database
body:
# TTK-01: CRUD on a real database

Target: Sprint 2
Ownership area: Developer: backend/full stack. Named assignee: pending team declaration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create, list, read, update and admin-delete gadgets through the backend API and UI.
- [ ] Records persist across refreshes and redeploys on the production database.
- [ ] Malformed IDs and invalid payloads return useful 4xx responses; authorization is tested.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Reviewed by at least one other teammate and merged to main through a PR.
- [ ] Required CI checks passed.
- [ ] Deployed and checked in the deployed environment.
- [ ] Link the issue, PR, CI run, commit and live verification evidence.

Current status: open GitHub backlog item. Initial implementation is proposed in #1; deployment and the course Definition of Done still require evidence.

title: [TTK-02] Non-trivial AI with backend output processing
body:
# TTK-02: Non-trivial AI with backend output processing

Target: Sprint 3
Ownership area: Developer: AI. Named assignee: pending team declaration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retrieve indexed specs with pgvector and answer gadget questions/comparisons with numbered citations.
- [ ] Backend processes the model result before responding: store answer/history, construct validated response/source objects, and check citation validity.
- [ ] Show a small evaluation set with measurable grounding and citation results; include unknown-spec and variant cases.
- [ ] CI uses mocked AI calls and evaluates output shape/grounding rather than exact prose.

# TTK-07: Graceful AI and request errors

Target: Sprint 3-4
Ownership area: Developer: AI/backend/frontend. Named assignee: pending team declaration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Save specs independently of AI availability; failed indexing preserves saved text.
- [ ] Test provider timeout, quota exhaustion, malformed/empty model output, and invalid client payloads.
- [ ] Query/index endpoints return safe, understandable failures rendered by the frontend.
- [ ] Keep input/token caps and rate limits; avoid provider calls for unrelated CI checks.
